summary: Establish pre-expansion consistency and health baseline
Pre-expansion consistency and health baseline
Approved rationale, ordered slices, preservation boundary, verification cadence, and stop conditions.
Superseded before execution because the first creation omitted typed autonomy fields; no implementation slice started.
Pre-expansion consistency and health baseline
Capturing the pre-expansion source, test, API, compatibility, bundle, browser, verification, and worktree baseline.

Captured revision, source/test scale, public seams, classified compatibility, build size, architecture status, exact equation and graph CLS failures, ResizeObserver symptom, and protected dirty-file hashes in an immutable baseline.
Classifying recent regressions by violated contract, detection gap, prevention gate, and canonical evidence.

Classified five evidence-backed regression families: representation substitution, semantic-identity substitution, late visual proof, lifecycle/reservation churn, and timing-policy leakage; assigned each to typed, architecture, browser, or human gates.
Auditing the actual semantic request-to-host path and every nearby construction or rendering path a fresh author could mistake for it.

Audited the end-to-end extension chain and found one concrete guidance conflict: the released governed canonical-construction public API is the new-work authority, while llm-animation-draft v2 is retained compatibility evidence. Classified adjacent internal, renderer, host, Article, and metadata paths.
Reconciling canonical vocabulary, model guidance, and construction documentation with the executable governed construction public seam.

Reconciled current LLM entrypoint, asset authoring spec, and system vocabulary with the released governed canonical-construction public API; explicitly demoted llm-animation-draft v2 to compatibility/research and added an executable guidance regression.
Inventorying declared public seams and classifying cross-owner deep imports without treating same-owner internal imports as violations.

Classified 13 named public modules by authority, added the omitted governed construction facade to the executable 19-surface caller ledger, and rejected raw deep-import counts as a repository-wide migration metric in favor of cross-owner ratchets.
Inventorying clocks, schedulers, mutable registries, lazy capability loaders, editor sessions, and stage lifecycle owners, with negative criteria for second authorities.

Added an executable 12-entry runtime authority inventory distinguishing pure sampling, playhead ownership, frame delivery, capability caches, adapter registries, presentation caches, and host lifecycles; classified four compatibility-managed owners and preserved the dashboard-only legacy exception outside runtime.
Strengthening every active compatibility entry with live caller, replacement, sunset, and retirement evidence rather than relying on name and status alone.

Required every active compatibility entry to carry live consumers, replacement source evidence, executable sunset tests, closure requirements, and an explicit retirement condition; the architecture gate now validates replacement references.
Attributing equation and graph catalogue CLS to exact pre-hydration and hydrated geometry changes before changing presentation.

Attributed the stable-reservation CLS failures to late KaTeX family and catalogue reading-font metrics plus a narrow dev-toolbar stylesheet ordering shift; enhanced failure evidence with source nodes and rectangles.
Applying resource reservation to the solve-x equation exemplar without changing its hydrated appearance or choreography.
Equation and catalogue reading fonts now settle at the lazy capability boundary before first visible stage mount; solve-x passes the unchanged 0.001 CLS ceiling with stable outer geometry.
Checking whether the graph defect shares the resource-reservation cause and applying only the common contract.

Graph SVG shares the KaTeX font-reservation cause; the same capability helper plus corrected dev-toolbar stylesheet ordering closes narrow-route CLS without graph-specific geometry or appearance changes.
Verifying capability loading, route closure, lazy boundaries, bundle budgets, type safety, and complete stage settlement after the shared reservation repair.

Closed the repair with 5/5 browser capability checks, the unchanged CLS ceiling, typecheck, 15 focused route/capability/preparation tests, architecture, and bundle gates; measured catalogue-route script is 111425 gzip bytes against 190000.
Migrating accepted linear solve from legacy recipe metadata to its existing typed equation presentation profile while preserving exact solve-x behavior.

Migrated canonical and teacher-detail linear solve assets from recipe metadata to typed equation presentation profiles; exact semantic serialization, direct seek, rewind, source lineage, focused tests, architecture, and typecheck pass.
Making every concrete equation-target catalogue asset explicitly select a typed presentation profile and ratcheting legacy metadata authoring to zero.

All 25 concrete equation-target catalogue assets now author typed profiles, including generated drafts, generated problems, comparisons, complex KaTeX samples, and inequality; a catalogue ratchet proves zero legacy metadata authors. Focused tests, typecheck, and architecture pass.
Tracing every decoder and legacy presentation metadata ingress across production, public exports, serialized assets, and tests before any deletion.

Proved the legacy decoder has no public export, serialized ingress, production author, or concrete catalogue dependency; all 25 equation-target assets carry typed profiles. Durable audit selects explicit stale-input failure and bounded retirement.
Retiring the decoder, eight compatibility entries, legacy-only tests and conformance branches, and the obsolete metadata authoring helper while retaining an explicit stale-key tombstone.

Deleted the 466-line legacy profile decoder and 200-line decoder suite, removed nine obsolete metadata compatibility paths plus the metadata authoring helper, and added explicit stale-key validation. The 251-test convergence suite, typecheck, and architecture gates pass.
Finishing the already-proven ownership move by recording the neutral animation policy as canonical and removing its migration debt.

Moved the equation presentation policy and branch-strategy reader into src/animation, updated every production/test caller, marked the compiler stage canonical, removed the ownership-debt entry, and updated the roadmap. No renderer resources entered the neutral owner.
Auditing sampled equation payload ownership against dependency direction and caller topology; moving only if the graph becomes simpler.

Separated canonical closed sampled payloads from the older public SDK EquationMotionFrame: the former are already neutral and canonical; the latter remains renderer-owned because a file-only move would reverse dependencies. Removed false debt and documented the justified retention; 36 focused tests, typecheck, and architecture pass.
Ratchet the newly migrated presentation-policy seam and touched production callers against renderer-owner and legacy-decoder bypasses.
